Guidance & outlook: The Company expects FY 26-27 growth to remain broadly consistent with the Company's demonstrated trajectory of around 25% revenue growth, underpinned by the same combination of specialisation, technology and disciplined execution that was delivered in the FY 25-26 performance.

Specialised logistics businesses - including freight forwarding, mining, coal logistics and fly-ash transportation - are expected to increase their cumulative share of revenues from 5.50% in FY 25-26 to around 12% in FY 26-27, a shift in the mix marked by superior margins and stronger revenue visibility.

More than 90% of FY 25-26 revenue was generated from large corporate customers, while the contribution of the top ten customers reduced from 84% in FY 23-24 to 73% in FY 25-26, reflecting a stronger diversification and reduced concentration risk.
Growth & demand: This 3x growth over the Indian economy was driven by higher freight volumes, deepening customer relationships and a rising contribution from specialised business verticals.

EBITDA grew 13% from INR 103.69 Crore in the previous year to INR 117.2 Crore, even as EBITDA margin moderated from around 20.4% to 18.4% - a deliberate trade-off, as higher market-hiring costs, toll expenses and insurance costs associated with business expansion were absorbed in the near term, the full benefit of which will progressively emerge.

Total income stood at INR 636.11 Crore, compared with INR 508.10 Crore in the previous year, reflecting growth in business volumes, fleet utilization, customer additions and expansion across key logistics corridors.
Margins & costs: The India logistics market, valued at USD 243.82 billion in 2025, is projected to expand to USD 429.02 billion by 2034, compounding at 6.48% annually, even as government initiatives aim to moderate logistics costs from around 14% of GDP today to single digits by 2030 - a reform that, if realised, would unlock incremental efficiency gains for organised logist…

Fleet utilisation remained at 82% in FY 25-26, with the management targeting approximately 85% through preventive maintenance, deeper OEM partnerships, improved route planning and greater return-load optimisation during the current financial year.

Following receipt of the Company's PESO licence, captive refuelling coverage is expected to rise from approximately 30% to nearly 50% of the fleet, giving the Company far greater control over one of its largest and most volatile operating costs.
Capex & expansion: Property, Plant and Equipment increased to INR 190.23 Crore from INR 153.01 Crore, reflecting continued investment in the Company's operating assets and fleet capabilities.
The Company deployed significant funds towards fleet expansion and other capital expenditure, resulting in net cash outflow from investing activities of approximately INR 126.03 Crore.
Property, Plant and Equipment increased to INR 190.23 Crore from INR 153.01 Crore, supporting the Company's capacity for future growth.
Balance sheet & cash: Operating cash flow remained healthy at INR 59.2 Crore, and IPO proceeds were deployed in line with stated objectives - principally towards fleet expansion and the strengthening of our operational capabilities.
With a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.14x against secured multi-year contracted revenues, the Balance Sheet remains positioned to fund the Company's growth.
Operating cash flow during FY 25-26 stood at INR 59.03 Crore, reflecting continued cash generation from operations despite increased working capital requirements.
Risks & challenges: India's middle-class is projected to expand to nearly 40% of the population by 2030, while the share of household spending devoted to non-food, discretionary categories - education, healthcare, consumer durables and services - rose steadily as the share of food in household budgets declined.

Risk management and financial discipline will remain central to execution as the Company navigates fuel price volatility, regulatory developments, competitive pricing pressures and changing customer requirements.

Nevertheless, threats such as fuel price volatility, pricing pressure from unorganized and fragmented players, driver shortages, increasing regulatory compliance requirements, cybersecurity risks aris-ing from greater IT integration and intensifying competition challenge the Company's growth trajec-tory.
